question: If people ask AI about faith and meaning, who should shape the answers it gives?
reflection: AI could free religious and community leaders for more time with people, while the deepest bonds stay human and face to face.

sources.subject: 200 bot accounts, one very real backlash

one_line: AI is reaching into personal and public life, from questions of faith to fierce local fights over data centres.

top_stories.title: Faith groups want a say in AI
top_stories.what: A report says chatbots now answer spiritual questions and help clergy with research and admin, and faith groups, governments and companies are building tools aligned with religious values.
top_stories.why: How people seek meaning and advice from AI is a rich topic for behavioural and cultural research.

top_stories.title: Data centre fight turns to jobs
top_stories.what: US building unions warn that slowing data centre projects could cost thousands of jobs, while X says about 200 foreign-linked bot accounts amplified local opposition.
top_stories.why: Public opinion on AI infrastructure is shaped by both real worries and organised influence, which surveys must separate.

top_stories.title: Automated researchers fix AI misbehaviour
top_stories.what: An Anthropic paper says AI research agents improved a model on all ten misbehaviour tests and beat experienced people on average within six hours at a fraction of the cost.
top_stories.why: If true, safety research could scale quickly, though human review of the results stays essential.

saudi_lens.text: Interest in AI tools aligned with religious values is directly relevant in Saudi Arabia, where trusted Islamic scholarship could guide how such tools are built and checked.

idea.title: How people seek guidance from AI
idea.pitch: A respectful study of when and why people ask AI about values and daily ethical choices, and what sources they trust in return.
idea.first_step: Draft an interview guide with eight open questions and review it with a cultural adviser.

idea_kids.title: Ask a person, ask a book, ask a machine
idea_kids.pitch: A classroom activity where children sort questions into those best asked to a parent or teacher, a book, or a computer, and explain why.
idea_kids.first_step: Write twenty child-friendly question cards and three sorting baskets.

watchlist.note: Open-sourced a framework that it says cuts some security fix cycles from weeks to hours.

watchlist.name: Hugging Face
watchlist.note: Selling a small, low-cost open robot built with Pollen Robotics.

watchlist.name: Google DeepMind
watchlist.note: Says its model predicts hurricane changes earlier than standard systems.

Anthropic's automated researchers are said to cost about $4 an hour against about $150 for people.

terms.definition: A group of automated social media accounts run together to make a view look more popular than it is.
When an AI system pursues goals or behaves in ways its makers did not intend.
The software around a model that gives it tools, memory and a loop for carrying out tasks.

concepts.summary: Faith groups seek influence over how chatbots handle religion.
Local opposition meets union pressure and foreign bot amplification.
AI agents now run parts of safety research on other models.
